items.title: Panorama of Eiffel Tower (Thomas A. Edison, Inc., 1900)
items.date: 1900 (filmed July 1900 at the Paris Exposition; copyright Thomas A. Edison 9 Aug 1900, D16385)
items.depicts: Ground-level shots under the Eiffel Tower at the 1900 Exposition: crowds walking beneath the great arch toward an ornate exposition building, then a slow vertical tilt from the arch up the whole tower to the summit and back down, ending on visitors walking toward the camera.
items.evidence: LoC record 00694266: summary '"Showing the entire height of this wonderful structure from the base of the dome and return, with the great Paris Exposition in the background, looking down Champs de Mars. A most realistic picture. 90 feet"--Edison films catalog, no. 105.'; notes 'Filmed July 1900, at the Paris Exposition in Paris, France.', 'Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 9Aug1900; D16385.', 'According to Edison film historian C. Musser, this film includes the earliest camera tilt found in surviving Edison productions.', 'Appearing: Lyman Howe (at about 1:20).'; subjects 'Tour Eiffel (Paris, France)', 'Palais de l'électricité (Exposition universelle, 1900, Paris, France)', 'Champ-de-Mars (Paris, France)'. Contributors: White, James H. (production); Thomas A. Edison, Inc; Paper Print Collection. Checked visually: tower clearly identifiable throughout 22-70 s.
items.active_area: Full 1440x1080 (4:3) frame is picture; no pillarbox/letterbox inside the file. In a 9:16 timeline use a 608x1080 vertical crop (x0~0.33 of width for most of the tilt; shift to ~0.42-0.84 for 43.5-47.3 where the upper shaft sits right of centre).
items.usable_ranges: (times in footage.mp4; add 13.042 for source.mp4) 1.0-6.0 static view under the tower's arch, crowd walking away toward the ornate exposition building, arch girders across top of frame (white ring blemish at 0.2-0.3 just before range); 26.0-31.0 tilt begins: arch rising out of frame, first-platform frieze fills frame (small specks, faint emulsion cracks from ~29); 31.0-36.0 tilt from first platform to second platform (hairline paper-print crazing visible in the sky from ~33); 43.5-47.3 upper shaft rising to the summit lantern against clean grey sky - best 'standing above Paris' shot (stop before 47.68-47.76: 3-frame frame-line slip with a dark horizontal bar); 59.5-65.0 tilt down from below the second platform to the first platform (white blotch at 58.65 just before range; light crazing); 65.0-69.5 tilt continues down past the first platform to the arch and crowd. Other: 9.5-15.0 second ground take under the arch (hard splice at 8.875); 71-96 visitors walking toward camera, tower legs only at top edge.
items.damage: Splice/jump cut at 8.875; frame-line slip 47.68-47.76; white blotch 58.65 and 41.5-43.0 (single-frame white spots); paper-print crazing (dark hairline cracks) in sky 33-43 and 50-60; constant fine grain and dust; last ~0.5 s brightens (end of roll). Transfer cadence: 16 fps material at 24 fps with every 3rd frame a duplicate (slight judder).

items.title: Scene from the elevator ascending Eiffel Tower (Thomas A. Edison, Inc., 1900)
items.date: 1900 (filmed July 1900 at the Paris Exposition; copyright Thomas A. Edison 9 Aug 1900, D16386)
items.depicts: Point-of-view from the roof of an elevator car climbing the Eiffel Tower: the tower's iron lattice girders sweep diagonally across frame while Exposition pavilions, roofs and crowds drop away below; passes the arched frieze of the first level with hanging lanterns; ends on a static high bird's-eye view down onto Exposition palaces.
items.evidence: LoC record 00694299: summary '"A marvelously clear picture taken from the top of the elevator of the Eiffel Tower during going up and coming down of the car. ... As the camera leaves the ground and rises to the top of the tower, the enormous white city opens out to the view of the astonished spectator. ... We furnish the ascent in 125 foot film"--Edison films catalog, no. 105.'; notes 'Filmed July, 1900 at the Paris Exposition in Paris, France.', 'Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 9Aug1900; D16386.', 'Duration: 1:59 at 16 fps.'; other titles 'Panoramic view from the Eiffel Tower, ascending and descending'; subjects 'Tour Eiffel (Paris, France)', 'Paris (France)--Aerial views'. This LoC copy is the ascent only (no descent seen). The LoC title card reads 'Effiel' (typo) - trimmed out.
items.active_area: Full 1440x1080 (4:3) frame is picture; no pillarbox/letterbox inside the file. Centre 9:16 crop (x 0.29-0.71) works for most ranges; for 79.5-83.0 crop left (x 0.0-0.42) to avoid the dark smear.
items.usable_ranges: (times in footage.mp4; add 12.542 for source.mp4) 2.0-6.5 diagonal tower girders sweeping past over ribbed glass pavilion roofs below (dark smears in corners); 21.5-25.0 looking down through the lattice onto a white pavilion with domed corners, street and people below (dark smear at 21.0 just before); 32.5-36.5 same white pavilion, girders crossing as the car climbs (clean-ish); 61.0-65.0 view out across Exposition rooftops and towers through passing girders (hairline crazing marks in sky); 79.5-83.0 the arched first-level frieze with hanging lanterns framing the ground far below - most clearly 'Eiffel Tower' frames (heavy dark diagonal smear over right half from ~80.5); 108.0-113.0 static high bird's-eye view straight down onto Exposition palaces at the end of the climb (crazing, dark mottling).
items.damage: Paper-print damage throughout: dark diagonal smears/shadows, emulsion crazing; near-black damaged frames 26.75-28.5, ~47, 59, 69.5-70, 84-90, 98-101 (avoid); lens/edge vignetting. Transfer cadence: 16 fps material at 24 fps with every 3rd frame duplicated.

items.title: Champs de Mars [Champ de Mars] (Thomas A. Edison, Inc., 1900)
items.date: 1900 (filmed July 1900 at the Paris Exposition; copyright Thomas A. Edison 9 Aug 1900, D16382)
items.depicts: Panning view along the Champ de Mars during the 1900 Exposition (women with parasols, pavilions), ending under the great arch of the Eiffel Tower with dense crowds walking toward the camera and an ornate exposition building framed in the arch.
items.evidence: LoC record 00694172: summary '"Shows all the prominent buildings on this thoroughfare, ending with a close view of the base of the Eiffel Tower, with the Trocadero Palace in the background. 135 feet"--Edison films catalog, no. 105.'; notes 'Filmed July 1900, at the Paris Exposition in Paris, France.', 'Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 9Aug1900; D16382.'; subjects 'Tour Eiffel (Paris, France)', 'Champ-de-Mars (Paris, France)', 'Palais du Trocadéro (Paris, France)'. CAUTION: the building seen through the arch looks like the same building as in 'Panorama of Eiffel Tower' (catalogued there as Palais de l'électricité); do not caption it as the Trocadero. Tower visible only from ~43.5 s.
items.active_area: 1440x1080 file; thin black bars top/bottom: active picture ~1440x1046 at y=16 (crop ~18 px top and bottom). No pillarbox. For 9:16 crop the arch reads best with x ~0.33-0.75.
items.usable_ranges: (times in footage.mp4; add 12.875 for source.mp4) 43.5-47.5 pan arrives at the tower: the great arch slides in from the left over crowds with parasols; 48.0-53.5 near-static view through the tower's arch, crowds of 1900 visitors walking toward camera, ornate building framed in the arch - sharpest tower shot of the set (white dust specks throughout); 54.0-57.0 same view, a visitor's large plaid umbrella sweeps close past the lens (playful, partially obstructs); 0.5-5.0 (no tower) women with parasols on the Champ de Mars, period atmosphere only.
items.damage: White dust specks throughout; thin vertical scratch lines in 15-40; no splices found (scene-change scan). Transfer is 24 fps without exact duplicate frames - every 3rd frame appears interpolated/blended (mild ghosting on fast movement).

items.title: Eiffel Tower from Trocadero Palace (Thomas A. Edison, Inc., 1900)
items.date: 1900 (filmed July 1900 at the Paris Exposition; copyright Thomas A. Edison 9 Aug 1900, D16387)
items.depicts: Static high view from the Trocadero toward the Eiffel Tower: the tower's legs and first level stand dark against a grey sky, cropped at the top of frame, with chimney smoke drifting, white Exposition pavilions and crowds below and a dark mass of trees on the right.
items.evidence: LoC record 00694193: summary '"The single camera position is from the top of a building identified as the Trocadero Palace; the camera is pointed toward the Eiffel Tower. The film shows only up to the first arch of the Eiffel Tower"--Early motion pictures.'; notes 'Filmed July 1900, at the Paris Exposition in Paris, France.', 'Copyright: Thomas A. Edison; 9Aug1900; D16387.', 'Duration: 1:11 at 16 fps.'; subjects 'Tour Eiffel (Paris, France)', 'Towers--France--Paris'.
items.active_area: 1440x1080 file; thin black bars top/bottom: active picture ~1440x1034 at y=22. No pillarbox. Tower sits at x ~0.25-0.65; 9:16 crop x ~0.24-0.66.
items.usable_ranges: (times in footage.mp4; add 12.958 for source.mp4) 1.0-7.5 static: tower base and first level, chimney smoke, white pavilions, crowd (flash frame at 7.79 just after); 9.0-15.0 same, smoke drifting; 20.0-26.0 same, steadiest exposure. Soft image with heavy white speckle over the whole frame in every range.
items.damage: Heavy fine white speckle throughout; single bright flash frame at 7.79; dark speckle bursts on right 36-41; large dark blotches covering much of frame 45.5-end (avoid). Transfer cadence: 16 fps at 24 fps with every 3rd frame duplicated.

notes: All four are Edison Manufacturing Co. actualities filmed July 1900 at the Paris Exposition Universelle (Library of Congress Paper Print Collection), i.e. the tower 11 years after completion - use them for 'seeing it standing above Paris' / later perception, never as 1887-1889 construction or 1889 Exposition footage. Each folder holds source.mp4 (LoC download, unaltered, H.264 1440x1080 24 fps with a silent AAC track and ~13 s LoC 'Preserved by' slate + title card at the head) and footage.mp4 (bare film only: slate, title card and LoC fades trimmed, video only, H.264 High CRF14 1440x1080 24 fps), plus meta.json with the catalogue record. subject_box is [x0, y0, x1, y1] as fractions of the 1440x1080 frame, sized as a full-height 9:16 crop window. Ranking for the edit: 1 Panorama of Eiffel Tower (hero tilt to the summit), 2 Elevator ascending (dramatic girders), 3 Champ de Mars (sharpest arch-and-crowd shot), 4 Trocadero (soft, speckled establishing view). Lumiere films (e.g. 1898 'Panorama pendant l'ascension de la Tour Eiffel') were not pursued: the four LoC items with an explicit rights statement already fill the 2-4 quota, and Lumiere copies online are usually Institut Lumiere restorations whose reuse status is not stated as public domain.
